one_line_contribution: Segment GEPA-optimized prompts into atomic clauses, estimate each clause's causal contribution both on its source task and when inserted into seven other tasks' baseline prompts, and use the resulting clause x target portability matrix to build a zero-rollout generic prefix whose value is priced in cold-start GEPA-rollout equivalents.
closest_prior_work: Two lines threaten it. (1) Min et al. 2022 (Rethinking the Role of Demonstrations) and Madaan & Yazdanbakhsh 2022 (Text and Patterns: For Effective Chain of Thought It Takes Two to Tango) already do component-wise counterfactual ablation of prompts and already report the exact dissociation this proposal predicts: the format/contract scaffold carries most of the benefit while the domain content contributes far less than its salience suggests. That is prediction (c) in a different wrapper. The proposal's answer -- 'those were hand-written taxonomies / demonstrations, we harvest from an optimizer' -- is close to the domain-swap move the track brief explicitly warns is scored as a modest delta. (2) Battle & Gollapudi 2024 on eccentric automatic prompts established that optimizer-discovered text is idiosyncratic and does not carry, which pre-empts part of the negative-transfer finding. GEPA/MIPROv2/OPRO/APE genuinely do not attribute gain to prompt parts, so the *object* (clause x target matrix over optimizer output) is new; the *finding* it is designed to produce is largely anticipated, so a reviewer will read a confirmed hypothesis as replication at a new granularity rather than discovery. The proposal's dismissal of SPoT/ATTEMPT is correct and not the problem.
strongest_objection: The central dissociation is measured with two non-comparable operators, so prediction (b) (Spearman ~0.0-0.3) and prediction (c) (content clauses transfer at delta <= 0) are close to guaranteed by the design rather than by any fact about portability. Experiment (4) estimates source contribution by *deleting* a clause from a co-adapted, jointly optimized prompt; experiment (5) estimates cross-task contribution by *appending* that same clause into a foreign prompt in a fixed slot. Deletion from a coherent optimized whole is superadditive -- removing a task-specific content clause can break references that other clauses depend on -- while a single appended sentence in a fixed slot is near-inert almost regardless of content. A low correlation between a deletion delta and an insertion delta is the expected result even if clause portability is perfectly predicted by source contribution, and the attenuation correction in experiment (6) does not touch this: it corrects for unreliability, not for the fact that the two quantities are different estimands. Consequently the paper's headline claim ('optimizers discover two kinds of text') is confounded with 'deleting differs from appending', and the mixed-model DeltaR^2 >= 0.15 for clause type is equally exposed, since clause type is strongly correlated with how self-contained a clause is and therefore with how much it survives being ripped out of context. A related, smaller instance of the same problem: the sham control in arm (5) is a semantically inverted clause, which for an output-contract clause ('always emit JSON' -> 'never emit JSON') is actively destructive against a format-sensitive parser rather than neutral, so the sham baseline is biased in exactly the direction that flatters the proposal's favored clause type.
what_would_fix_it: Add a symmetric arm: insert each clause into its OWN task's baseline prompt, in the same fixed slot, on the same attribution set, and define source contribution as that insertion delta. Then the dissociation test in (6) compares insertion-to-insertion, and any residual low correlation is about portability rather than about operator. Keep the leave-one-clause-out numbers as a secondary, explicitly non-comparable measure of co-adaptation. Second, pre-register how prediction (e) is evaluated: 'removing format-compliance-driven items from the metric' is undefined for exact-match GSM8K/BBH/MBPP, and it needs to be a concrete lenient-parse re-scoring rule fixed before the matrix is computed, otherwise the accuracy-vs-contract split is decided after seeing the results. Third, replace the sham control for contract clauses with a neutral-but-plausible contract clause naming a different, unenforced format, so the control is not destructive by construction. Fourth, fit the mixed model with crossed random effects for source task and target task; with 8 tasks the effective n for a type-level claim is closer to 8 than to the 15-40 cells the power calculation assumes, and the quoted 1.2-point detectable effect is optimistic under that clustering.
missing_baseline: A zero-measurement LLM-authored library: give the frontier reflector model the 7 source-task optimized prompts and ask it to write a generic transferable prefix at the same token cap, with no clause segmentation, no attribution, and no cross-task scoring. This is the direct competitor to the entire ~168k-generation measurement apparatus, and it is strictly stronger than the plan's baseline (iii), which is hand-written *without seeing any optimization run* and therefore does not test whether the expensive causal estimation -- as opposed to merely reading the optimized prompts -- was necessary. If the LLM-summarized prefix matches the measured library, the paper's method reduces to an expensive way to reproduce a one-call summary. Also missing: a multi-source whole-prompt warm start (concatenated or LLM-merged prompts from all 7 sources); baseline (ii) transfers only the single best source prompt, which is the weakest form of the obvious cheap alternative.
preprint_collision: There is no collision check. The field is empty and the Related Work section states outright that all citations are unverified and the literature-search backend was unavailable, so the submission reports zero searches of any kind, indexed or preprint. Under the standard applied here that is a weakness, not a neutral: novelty is asserted, not established. This matters more than usual because the anchor method, GEPA (Agrawal et al., 2025), is itself a recent preprint, and the highest-risk collision zone is precisely its 2025-2026 follow-up literature -- analyses of what optimized prompts actually contain, ablations of GEPA/MIPRO-returned instructions, and reusable system-prompt/meta-prompt library papers -- none of which the authors have looked at. I cannot name a specific preprint that already makes this claim from the text under review, but the absence of any search means the authors cannot either, and a reviewer who does spend ten minutes on arXiv is likely to surface a component-ablation or transferable-instruction-library paper from the last two quarters. This should be resolved before the novelty claim in the Related Work section ('the new object here is a clause x target portability matrix') can be credited.
